text:
anna: Nightly gpu-shard-7 just hit a red on the model-smoke matrix. Multiple pods failed with a kernel assertion followed by OOM in the same minute. Posting a small log snippet and job info. link: https://ci.internal/red/12345

ci-bot: Job 12345 shard=7 failed: kernel_assertion + OOM. Collected logs at /artifacts/12345/shard7.tar.gz

anna: excerpt from dmesg (from the failing node):
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3a:00): 31, PID=2345, GPU=0, CC=8.0
[ 1234.568012] gpu0: kernel assertion at src/alloc.c:412
[ 1234.568130] oom-killer: killing process 5678 (trainer) score 1024
```

raj: ugh. is this the driver-canary node group? last week we saw a driver flip on canary. @ming can you check the node driver?

ming: checking now — node image lists nvidia-driver=535.86.05, CUDA 12.2. I saw a similar assertion when we rolled the 540.* preview (different cluster). Two quick asks: 1) attach nvidia-smi and pmon output from the failing run, 2) can you requeue with DEBUG_GPU=1 so we get per-process memory snapshots?

sam: adding the minimal commands we want in the rerun:
```bash
# run on the node (or via debug container)
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,memory.free,memory.used --format=csv
nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv -i 0
sudo dmesg | tail -n 80
cat /proc/5678/smaps | grep -i rss || true
```

sam: also please enable GPU_TRACE=1 in the CI job so the runtime prints kernel launch stacks.

anna: queued a rerun with DEBUG_GPU=1 and GPU_TRACE=1 (rerun id 12345.1). Also uploaded the artifact link above.

ops-bot: Rerun scheduled: 12345.1 on pool=hetero-gpu-debug, MIG disabled. ETA ~6m

raj: thanks. if the rerun shows steady memory growth before the assertion it's probably a shared vram leak (we've seen cross-process growth when the allocator doesn't free on early error). If it spikes immediately then it's likely an alignment/kernel bug.

ming: quick note: hardware telemetry shows memory fragmentation increased prior to crash on last run. I want a bisect across driver versions 535 -> 540 across the last 3 canaries. Can we pin a bisect job?

anna: yes, filing a bisect job now — bisect-12345 (driver versions: 532.41, 533.05, 535.86.05, 538.13, 540.10). We'll run the model-smoke matrix across the set.

sam: if anyone's triaging locally, here's a tiny repro harness that allocs 90% of VRAM then does concurrent kernels — might trigger the assertion quickly:
```python
# alloc_leak.py (toy)
import torch
x = torch.empty((1024,1024,200), device='cuda')
for i in range(200):
    torch.randn_like(x, device='cuda') * 1.0001
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
```

raj: nice. can we also try the rerun with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get synchronous kernel failures (will slow but helps stack traces)?

anna: done — rerun updated with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1.

ci-bot: Rerun 12345.1 started on node gpu-debug-17. Artifacts streaming to /artifacts/12345.1/

ming: preliminary from the debug rerun: memory gradually increases over ~30s then kernel assert triggers. Per-process memory shows trainer (pid 5678) and helper workers steadily increasing used_memory. Attaching pmon snapshot in artifacts.

raj: that leans toward a leak. Could be our allocator caching shards across kernels. @sam can you grep for missing free paths in allocator code? I'll spin a small instrumented run to free after every op to see if leak goes away.

sam: will do. quick question for infra: do we have a way to force a single-job per GPU on canary so we can rule out cross-process contamination?

ops-bot: You can set node annotation `redwood/infer/exclusive=true` in the job spec; cluster autoscaler will honor it for debug pools.

anna: thanks — I'll launch an exclusive debug run next. If the exclusive run still grows memory then it's internal to process; if it stays stable, we have an interleaving problem.

raj: timeline: run exclusive debug + instrumented free by sam. If both indicate leak, we'll escalate to infra for driver bisect and open a bug against allocator team. If exclusive is clean, we'll run a stress with helper workers one-by-one to find the contaminated process.

ming: FYI I'm also collecting kernel modules + trace logs (ftrace) from the node and will upload to /artifacts/12345.traces.tar.gz once complete.

anna: +1. I'll follow up in this thread with the exclusive run link. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: quick note — added a lightweight allocation guard in allocator branch `alloc/guard-leak-12345` to try on repro. Will post PR link when ready.

ci-bot: Rerun 12345.1 completed: failed with same pattern. Artifacts: /artifacts/12345.1/final.tar.gz

anna: received — moving to the exclusive run now.

ops-bot: Bisect job bisect-12345 queued across drivers [532.41,533.05,535.86.05,538.13,540.10]. ETA ~2h.

raj: thanks. keeping this thread for updates. If anyone finds a fast mitigation (e.g., pinning driver to 535 or disabling helper workers) post here.

ming: uploaded traces. early look doesn't show kernel page fault spikes before assertion — more consistent with user-space leak.

anna: exclusive run link: https://ci.internal/red/12345.excl — running now.

sam: PR: https://git.internal/r/alloc/guard-leak-12345 — includes extra frees and a debug counter. If you can run that variant on the exclusive job it might confirm.

anna: queued exclusive run with alloc/guard-leak-12345. Will report back in ~10m.

raj: good plan. thanks everyone.

ming: pinging infra on driver-bisect status: @ops-bot any updates?

ops-bot: bisect-12345 job started. logs will be in /artifacts/bisect-12345/ as they arrive.

anna: closing loop for now — will post final result once bisect and exclusive runs finish.

sam: cheers.
